_strategy.note: 8-team PPR blueprint: take an elite WR (Nacua/Chase) in Round 1 over RBs, secure a top RB in Rounds 2-3, and grab a premium TE by Rounds 6-7 because the drop-off after Tyler Warren is 'major' in shallow leagues; double up on one team's pass-catchers freely after Round 10.

Avoid QBs in Rounds 1-3 (Josh Allen is the only Round 2 consideration); Lamar Jackson and Drake Maye are the Round 4 targets, then Burrow/Daniels/Hurts in Round 5, and dual-threat QBs keep falling into Rounds 7-9.

From picks 1-2 go Hero RB (Gibbs or Bijan) then two WRs or a WR plus Bowers/McBride in Rounds 2-3; from picks 3-6 build WR-WR or WR-TE with Chase/Nacua/St. Brown/JSN; wait on QB (Herbert or Caleb Williams in Round 7) and take late fliers on MarShawn Lloyd, Jonah Coleman, Keaton Mitchell.

_strategy.source: ESPN — Eric Karabell (Do Not Draft list)
_strategy.note: Position depth at QB makes Josh Allen in Round 2 a prohibitive opportunity cost; 2025's rookie-WR class (Tate, Lemon, Concepcion, Cooper Jr., Boston) will be overdrafted — historically only 2 of 8 top rookie WRs finished top-50 — so veterans Wan'Dale Robinson, Jordan Addison and Quentin Johnston are better value.
Top-tier QBs (Allen, Lamar, Maye) are overpriced when elite RBs and WRs are still on the board because 'the quarterback position is mega-deep this year.'

Across 28 drafts Eisenberg's most-rostered players were MarShawn Lloyd (Round 10+ after the Jacobs exempt-list news), D'Andre Swift (value up after Monangai's knee injury), Jadarian Price (Round 5), Luther Burden III (Round 5 after the groin scare) and DJ Moore (Round 4).
